text:
rachel: quick food-for-thought: what if we ship some large shards as pre-gzipped .safetensors.gz to save bandwidth and let clients stream-decompress into the KV warmup path? pros: less bytes over wire for cold starts. cons: mmap loaders and partial reads. thoughts?

anya: interesting. main worry is random access & mmap. many of our loaders assume direct offsets into the file. gzipped objects break that. how would streaming decompression map to per-tensor offsets?

rachel: two ideas: 1) produce a tiny uncompressed index sidecar with tensor offsets in the *uncompressed* address space so client can know which compressed window contains a tensor. 2) chunk the gzip into independent concatenated gzip members aligned to a window size (e.g., 4MB) so you can decompress window-by-window without backtracking.

pavan: concatenated gzip members are nice; you can seek to window boundary, fetch that member, decompress it and verify. but support across CDNs and object stores for partial fetches of members needs careful Content-Range handling. also we need per-member checksums and signatures for provenance.

anya: agreed on signatures. operationally we should keep on-disk safetensors layout invariant for on-prem customers who rely on mmap. so gzipped shards would be a separate distribution artifact, not replacing canonical .safetensors files. server advertises via header X-Weight-Compressed: gzip; X-Weight-Index: <url>.client can prefer compressed variant when streaming allowed.

rachel: right, this is an alternate transport artifact. client warmup flow proposal: 1) fetch index sidecar (small) OR index-hash in header; 2) issue range fetches for compressed members that contain hot tensors; 3) stream-decompress into provisional KV entries; 4) verify per-member checksum and signature; 5) promote provisional entries to verified. fallback: if index missing or signature invalid, fall back to uncompressed shard.

pavan: two perf notes: decompressing on the client adds CPU & memory pressure. we should allow server-side decompress and offer both compressed and uncompressed endpoints. also include a server hint header X-Weight-DecodeCostMs to let clients decide.

anya: runtime API changes: provisional flag + tombstone/unpin, and an API to atomically promote a set of warmup entries once checks pass. also emit metrics: decompress_cpu_ms, provisional_promote_latency, compressed_bytes_saved.

infra-bot: canary deploy: eng-ml/warmup-experiments -> compressed-transport-canary @ 04:15 UTC.

rachel: edge-case: delta-updates/patches on gzipped streams are harder. suggest we support gzipped distributed only for immutable model snapshots; deltas keep using uncompressed chunked artifacts.

pavan: +1. also add tests for CDNs that rewrite ranges and for curl/Range edgecases. sample header example to include in RFC:

```
X-Weight-Compressed: gzip
X-Weight-Index: https://objstore/models/m1/shard-000.safetensors.gz.index
X-Weight-DecodeHint: {"member_size":4194304,"verify":"sig-v1"}
```

anya: ok I'll fold this into the RFC draft and include canary plan + tests. thanks, concise and actionable.
